summary: The team is juggling a website redesign, SEO prioritization for Asia Star and Intelligent China, and event prep for Tech in Asia, with urgent IT fixes and speaker confirmations needed this week.
summaryDetail: The most pressing issue is resolving email login issues by updating authentication codes on all devices, a quick fix that's blocking team communication. Meanwhile, the knowledge website redesign is moving forward: the team has decided to drop the videos panel, adopt a two-menu structure, and blend Joseph's design elements to surface more articles and indices—feedback on his design is due soon. On the marketing front, Asia Star and Intelligent China are the top SEO priorities, with Berkeley as a secondary focus; work is underway on target audience profiles and conversion tracking. For upcoming events, the Tech in Asia engagement on Sep 15-16 is heating up: the Luma page is launching, the agenda is being finalized (including removing Dean Xiang's speech), and preferred speakers have been selected—confirmations are needed. Additionally, Global Foundation membership renewal and a collaboration call with Natalia are on the radar, along with forwarding an energy company contact for the EV program.

decisions.text: Remove the videos panel from the knowledge website homepage.
Integrate videos into topic-based sections rather than a separate category.
Adopt the two-menu structure with a school menu and a knowledge menu.
Incorporate elements from Joseph's design to display more articles and highlight indices.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for marketing and SEO.
Consider Berkeley as a third priority, but with lesser emphasis.
Put US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia) on hold for the first quarter.
